HON'BLE MR ANANDA KUMAR TIWARI
 (JUDICIAL MEMBER)

The instant appeal
u/s 41
of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (hereinafter referred to Act of 2019) is
at the behest of Sri Arya Sumant impeaching order dt. 11/12/2023 passed by Hon'ble District
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Unit II (hereinafter referred to Hon'ble District
Commission) in complaint case no. CC/343/2021 which was dismissed on contest against the OPs
with cost of Rs. 1000/-.
It is the case of the Appellant that he purchased one iPhone 12 on 5th November, 2020 under
customer No. 919029 being model name iPhone 12 , Row 64GB, Red, IMEI/serial no.
353053112849874 for a price of Rs. 79900/-. It is stated that from the date of purchase said phone was
running smoothly but after few months (June 2021) the Appellant started facing problem with the
sound system of the phone and for a few days the Appellant ignored the same but gradually the
problem increased and from the morning of 22nd August, 2021 the Appellant failed to hear the voices
of the callers while receiving phone calls.
According to the Appellant he thereafter went to the Respondent no. 2 being the authorised
service centre of Respondent no. 1 and the Respondent no. 2 issued a service record dt. 23rd August
2021 under the head "issue reported by customer" that "no receivers sound" and also that "cosmetic
condition of product: multiple dents on edges and dent on back panel. It is stated that the Appellant
handed over the phone in the custody of Respondent no. 2 for repair and left the service centre. It is
the further case of the Appellant that after passage of considerable amount of time he was informed by
the staff of Respondent no. 2 that they were unable to open the phone and repair the defect since there
were multiple dents on it but they refused to mention the reason for non-repairing by e-mail and
insisted the Appellant to collect the phone from their custody.
It is the further case of the Appellant that being aggrieved by the non-action of the Respondent
No 2, he searched in the computer complaint logging site of the Respondent and while surfing found a
press release dt. 27th August, 2021 in connection with iPhone 12 and iPhone 12 pro service program
for no sound issues-Apple support and on opening the window learnt the following:
"Apple has determined that a very small percentage of iPhone 12 and iPhone 12 pro devices
may experience sound issues due to a component that might fail on the receiver module. Affected
devices were manufactured between October 2020 and April 2021.
If your iPhone 12 or iPhone 12 Pro does not emit sound from the receiver when you make or
receive calls, it may be eligible for service.
Apple or an Apple Authorized Service Provider will service eligible devices, free of charge.
iPhone 12 mini and iPhone 12 Pro Max models are not part of this program.
If your iPhone 12 or iPhone 12 Pro has any damage which impairs the ability to complete the
repair, such as cracked screen,that issue will need to be resolved prior to the service. In some cases,
there may be a cost associated with the additional repair.
Additional Information

 Apple may restrict or limit repair to the original country or region of purchase.
This worldwide Apple program doesn't extend the standard warranty coverage of the iPhone 12
or iPhone 12 Pro.
The program covers affected iPhone 12 or iPhone 12 Pro devices for 2 years after the first retail
sale of the unit."
It is stated that from the bare perusal of the press release it was established that there was
manufacturing defect and the phone was from the defective batch of iPhone. The Appellant stated that
finding no alternative he filed the complaint praying for a direction upon the opposite parties to
replace the defective mobile phone with a new one in terms of the press release dated 27th August,
2021 or repair the existing phone and extend the warranty period or to refund the amount along with
interest and compensation, but the complaint case was dismissed after contest.
Being aggrieved by the order of dismissal the Appellant preferred this appeal on the ground that
Hon'ble District Commission failed to consider the press release of the Respondent No 1 where the
manufacturer himself admitted about the defect and the Respondent No 2 being authorized service
centre fails to act upon it. It is further stated that the Respondent have made frivolous allegations about
the multiple dents of the body of the said phone through there was no dent on the back panel of the
said phone and there could never be dent on the back panel as the same was made of fragile substance
like glass. The further ground for preferring the appeal was that the Hon'ble District Commission
could not visualise the case made out by the Respondent in collusion with each other and further that
Hon'ble District Commission failed to consider the email dt. 28th September, 2021 stating
"congratulations, your iPhone 12 is ready to be collected by you" and after receiving the e-mail, the
Appellant vide e-mail dated 21/09/2021 enquired whether the iPhone was repaired or not and there
was no reply from the Respondent and further that Hon'ble District Commission failed to consider that
that the Respondent No 2 could not produce any evidence in support of their reason for refusal of
repair. Contending the above and other grounds stated in the memorandum of appeal the Appellant
prayed to set aside the order passed by Hon'ble District Commission and allow the complaint case
being CC/343/2021.
After filing of the appeal notice was issued to the Respondents, however, the Respondent no. 1
only appeared and filed BNA and Ld Advocates for both parties were heard.
The Respondent no. 1 in the BNA stated that the Appellant purchased the mobile phone on
05/11/2020 and on 23/08/2021 after using the said phone for 9 months without any issues, the
Appellant approached Respondent no. 2 being the apple authorised service provider of Respondent no.
1 and informed that the iPhone has issueswith receiver sound. It is stated that the technicians of
Respondent no.2 received said iPhone and issued service record dated 23/08/2021 to the Appellant
mentioning that multiple dents on edges and dent on back panel. It is further stated that Respondent
No 2 informed the Appellant that said iPhone cannot be repaired in-warranty as it has physical damage
and offered a paid replacement but Appellant refused to pay for the replacement and contended that he
has not caused any dent to the iPhone. It is further stated that the Appellant was also asked to collect
the iPhone but instead of collecting the phone he insisted for free repair of the iPhone and as a part of
procedure the Respondent no. 2 has captured pictures of the iPhone which depicts multiple dents on
the edges and back of the phone and the original photographs were produced as Annexure A series to
the written version filed by the Respondent.
It is further stated that on 27/08/2021 the Respondent no. 1 determining that a very small
percentage of iPhone 12 and iPhone 12 pro models manufactured between October, 2020 and April
2021 could experience sound issues published advertisement which was produced by the Appellant at
annexure C to the complaint for getting the iPhone model repaired free of cost in spite of the fact that
it was mentioned in the advertisement that if the iPhone models has any damage which impairs the
ability to complete the repair, then such issue needs to be resolved prior to the service and such
additional repair would be associated with cost. It is stated that the Respondent no. 1 clearly informed
the Appellant that due to the physical damage like multiple dents it cannot be repaired in-warrantee but
theAppellant was reluctant to accept the fact that he has caused multiple dent on the iPhone.
It is stated that thereafter the Appellant filed the Complaint case which was rightly dismissed
by the Hon'ble District Commission and the Appellant filed the appeal.
We have heard the argument of both sides at length and also have gone through the final
order/judgment passed by Hon'ble District Commission. We find that Hon'ble Commission observed
"so, considering the entire evidence on record, this Commission is of view that when the complainant
brought the subject iPhone to the OP no. 2 being the authorised service centre Kolkata, the subject
phone was already damaged and there were multiple dents on edge and dent on back panel. It was
mentioned in the service record (annexure B) and the complainant put his signature on the record
without raising any objection thereon". Hon'ble Commission while passing the order further observed
that the subject phone was damaged either by mishandling or misuse by the complainant or any
unauthorized personnel prior to submission of the same before the service centre in that case the Ops
are in no way responsible to refund the amount or to give free repairing service to the complainant.
We have also gone through the copy of service record and the terms and conditions annexed
thereto. We find that while handing over the iPhone for service, the Respondent No 2 mentioned in the
 service record that multiple dents on edges and dent on back panel and the copy of the said service
record was accepted by the complainant by putting his signature. The condition of the iPhone as
mentioned is typed in computer and not handwritten and it cannot be also said that it was written after
the customer signed in the service record. We have also gone through the clause 7 of the terms and
condition of the service, which clearly mentions that "The AASP shall not be responsible for damages
during service to any product, which has been tampered or modified by unauthorized personnel before
submission at the service center" and Hon'ble District Commission mentioned and discussed this
clause in the impugned judgment.
We have also gone through the copies of email correspondences in between the parties. Email
dated 18/09/2021 forwarded by the Respondent No 2 to the Appellant goes as follows-
"Congratulations! Your iPhone 12 is ready to be collected by you". In reply the Appellant asked "What
do you mean by this? Is the phone repaired or not? The Respondent No 2 informed the Appellant that
the email dated 18/09/2021 was generated due to the long pendency to process the repair. It was
further intimated to the Appellant to confirm whether he wish to undertake the repair of the iPhone by
making payment or in the alternative was requested to collect the iPhone. We find that in reply to said
email by the Respondent No 2, the Appellant stated that there is no physical damage to the phone
though the fact remains that when the iPhone was handed over to the Respondent No 1, the Appellant
signed in the Service record accepting that there was dent in the edges and back panel. After going
through the complete set of conversation in between the Appellant and Respondent No 1 by e-mail, we
are not impressed by the point of argument made by Ld Advocate for the Appellant that by email the
Respondent informed them that the IPhone was ready to be collected after repair.
In view of the facts before us, we are of the opinion that there is no merit in the Appeal No
28/2024 preferred by the Appellant and as such the same is liable to be dismissed.
Hence it is

 ORDERED
 That the Appeal filed by the Appellant bearing No A/28/2024 is dismissed on contest without
any order as to cost. The impugned order dated 11/12/2023 passed by Hon'ble District Consumer
Disputes Redressal Commission, Kolkata, Unit-II is hereby affirmed.
A copy of this order be provided to the parties free of costs as mandated by rules.
The order be uploaded on the website of Commission for perusal of the parties.
A copy of this order be also forwarded Hon'ble District Consumer Disputes Redressal
Commission, Kolkata, Unit-II and the File be consigned to record room along with the copy of this
order. The appeal is disposed of and pending application(s) if any are also disposed of.
